In evaluating 1920s Victorians and Craftsman bungalows throughout Inman Park, our inspection teams routinely encounter distinct building science challenges: ungrounded knob-and-tube junction splices concealed under blown-in attic insulation, sagging heart-pine floor joists from unvented crawlspaces, and crushed original clay sewer pipes.

We published a dedicated diagnostic guide specifically tailored for Inman Park historic home maintenance and pre-purchase due diligence:

hook: Recent surge in flipped home purchases across Sandy Springs, Dunwoody, and Brookhaven concealing unpermitted hazards.
pitchSubject: Story Pitch: The Hidden Electrical & Foundation Risks Inside North Metro Flipped Homes
pitchBody:
Hi Rough Draft Atlanta Editorial Team,

With home prices pushing North Metro buyers into recently renovated properties across Sandy Springs, Dunwoody, and Brookhaven, buyers are paying record premiums for homes that look brand-new on the surface.

However, behind the shiplap and quartz countertops, our inspection teams are discovering an alarming pattern: over 65% of fast-flipped homes exhibit unpermitted electrical panel double-taps, non-trapped plumbing vents, and fresh drylock paint applied over active foundation shears.

Certified Master Inspector Christopher Boykin has compiled field data and thermal imaging case studies illustrating what North Metro buyers must verify before closing:
https://www.fhinspectionsatl.com/blog/hidden-dangers-of-flipped-homes-atlanta-inspection-guide

Christopher is available for a quick interview or commentary on red flags buyers should watch for during open houses this weekend.

Best regards,

Christopher Boykin, CMI®
Foresight Home Inspections | 678-480-2110
